page: Microsoft Azure F8amds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine driven by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor on the x86_64 architecture, managed by Microsoft Hyper-V. The configuration provides 8 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading (1 thread per core) operating at a 4.5 GHz base frequency. Cache allocation includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity stands at 64.0 GB, providing an 8.0 GB per-core allocation. Storage is bundled directly via an integrated 944 GB local NVMe SSD, while hardware accelerators such as GPUs are not included. CPU vector instruction support is broad, encompassing AVX, AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16), and cryptographic hardware extensions.

Benchmark evaluation shows exceptional single-threaded CPU capability alongside moderate multi-threaded throughput. In single-core stress-ng testing, the instance scored 3715.99, placing it in the top 10% of tested instances. This is supported by top-tier single-threaded compression performance, recording 40.09 GB/sec in gzip and 17.83 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Multi-core performance aligns with the median tier, achieving 29644.86 in multi-core stress-ng and 24622.3 on the PassMark CPU test. Large-block memory bandwidth measures 53.85 GB/sec for uncached reads and 33.95 GB/sec for writes. The machine achieves 23.95 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks and runs small 135M parameter LLM text generation at a top-tier 362.66 tokens/sec, though LLM processing drops sharply on larger 70B parameter models due to the 8-core allocation limit.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F8amds_v7 provides strong resource density by pairing dedicated high-frequency AMD execution units with generous memory and low-latency NVMe scratch capacity. The 1:8 core-to-memory ratio and high-speed local disk mitigate memory pressure in data-heavy tasks without forcing an upgrade to higher-vCPU tiers. The primary tradeoff lies in raw parallel throughput, as aggregate multi-core scaling is capped by the 8 physical cores. This profile is optimal for single-thread-limited computing, data compression pipelines, in-memory caches like Redis, localized database engines, and lightweight model inference.
description: Microsoft Azure F8amds_v7 is a compute-focused instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with 8 dedicated physical cores operating at 4.5 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provisions 64.0 GB of memory (8.0 GB per core) and includes a 944 GB local NVMe SSD, while omitting hardware GPU acceleration. Architectural features include 32 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction sets such as AVX-512 and SHA_NI. Benchmark evaluation reveals top-tier single-core performance, evidenced by top 10% results in single-thread stress-ng runs, gzip compression reaching 40.09 GB/sec, and fast text generation on compact 135M language models. Multi-core compute and memory bandwidth throughput perform in the median range, with throughput declining sharply on 70B parameter models due to core count constraints. Offering a balanced ratio of 8 GB memory per vCPU and fast local disk, the F8amds_v7 is well suited for memory-intensive batch jobs, compression pipelines, in-memory caching, and database workloads requiring local NVMe scratch storage.
